refuted.claim: note1410.txt's documented instruction-length map is confirmed by the file contents: each entry is 'op 11111 22222 / op 33333 / op' followed by two halts, so each address exercises the 3 legal instruction lengths (11, 6, 1).
refuted.why: The 11/6/1 pattern holds only for ops with no d-character. I decoded ilentest.cor directly. Ops that carry a d-modifier are 12/6/1, the channel-status and unconditional branches are 7 only (no 6 or 1 form present), Store Address Register is 7 only, and Halt is 6/1. Decoded bytes: 00100 '_A1111122222 _A33333 _A' (11/6/1); 00700 '_D1051711111 22222 +' -> '_D1111122222+ _D33333 _D' (12/6/1); 01300 '_B1111122222D _B33333 _B' (12/6/1); 01100 T, 01400 W, 01500 V all identical 12/6/1; 01200 '_J11111A _X22222B _R33333D' (three separate 7-char instructions, no chained or 6-char forms); 01600 '_G11111A' (7 only); 02000 '_.11111 _. _.' (6/1). IBM A22-0526-3 gives the legal lengths per op: Add/Subtract/ZA/ZS 'L = 1 or 11' plus the one-field L=6 form; Multiply/Divide 'L = 1, 6, or 11'; Move D 'L = 1, 6 or 12'; BCE B 'L = 1, 6 or 12'; Branch J 'L = 1 or 7'.
refuted.correction: The ilentest/insttest length blocks exercise whatever lengths are legal for that particular op, not a uniform 11/6/1. Correct groupings: 11/6/1 for A S ? ! @ % Z E C , lozenge / ; 12/6/1 for D B W V T (ops with a d-character); 7 only for J X R (branches) and G (SAR); 6/1 for . (Halt). An implementer using these blocks as a decode oracle must key expected instruction length off the op, not off a constant.
refuted.source: Decoded https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cube1us/1410/master/Core/ilentest.cor at 00100/00200/00500/00700/01100/01200/01300/01400/01500/01600/01700/01800/01900/02000/02100 (4-byte little-endian, low 6 bits through Jaeger's bcd_ascii) against IBM 1410 Principles of Operation A22-0526-3, http://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/A22-0526-3_1410_princOps.pdf, instruction-form/Timing 'L =' lines for Add, Subtract, Multiply, Divide, Move, BCE and Branch Conditionally (pp. 19-26, 45)

refuted.claim: The op character actually stored at 00500 ... is BCD 12 (bits 8-4), which Jaeger's own table renders as @.
refuted.why: The op-code identification is right but the rendering statement is wrong. Jaeger's bcd_ascii[12] is '\'' (apostrophe), with the comment '12    84    - at sign @ or quote'. SIMH's mem_to_ascii[014] is likewise '\'' with i7000_defs.h commenting '#define CHR_QUOT 014 /* Also @ */'. Neither table renders BCD 12 as '@'.
refuted.correction: BCD 12 (8-4 bits) IS the 1410 Multiply op code, and IBM prints it as '@' (A22-0526-3 Multiply instruction form: 'MNEMONIC M / OP CODE @'). But both emulators render that code position as an ASCII apostrophe, not '@'. Anyone diffing printed output or disassembly text between the two must expect ' where the manual shows @.
refuted.source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cube1us/1410/master/ubcd.cpp bcd_ascii[64] entry 12; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rcornwell/sims/master/I7000/i7010_sys.c mem_to_ascii[64] entry 014; op code confirmed in IBM A22-0526-3 http://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/A22-0526-3_1410_princOps.pdf Multiply instruction form

refuted.claim: i7010 can boot from cards: cdr_boot calls chan_boot ... i.e. it reproduces the 1402 Load key ... So `att cdr0 deck.txt` + `boot cdr0` is a working card-only entry path if a deck existed.
refuted.why: This is exactly the 1401/1410/7010 conflation the project needs to avoid. The Load key is a 7010 feature, not a 1410 one. IBM C28-0351-5 (1410/7010 Operating Guide) states plainly: 'Use of the IBM 7010 Load Key: The procedures above can be used on both the 1410 and the 7010. On the 7010, the Load key can be used instead of entering the read instruction into locations 00000-00011.' Every initialization table in that manual is split into 'Using 7010 Load Key' and 'Not using 7010 Load Key'; the not-using path is the 1410 path and it requires the operator to hand-key a 12-character read instruction into 00000-00011 and press computer reset + start. CC01A's own loading procedure does the same thing ('Display and Alter Locations 00000-00011 as follows: RL%B000011$.'). The '1402 Load key' phrasing is 1401 vocabulary; the 1402 Load key is the 1401's.
refuted.correction: SIMH's `boot cdr0` models the 7010 Load key (Load toggle switch, Card position), a feature a strict 1410 does not have. On a strict 1410 the only entry path is manual: deposit a 10-character L/M I/O instruction plus surrounding characters into 00000-00011, computer reset, start. If the project's oracle is meant to be strict-1410-faithful, `boot` is out of scope and the equivalent is scripted DEPOSITs into 00000-00011 followed by run from 00000.
refuted.source: IBM 1410/7010 Operating Guide C28-0351-5, http://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/C28-0351-5_1410_operGuide.pdf, Tables I and II 'Using 7010 Load Key' / 'Not using 7010 Load Key' (p.7) and 'Use of the IBM 7010 Load Key' (p.32); CC01A p.004 2.xx.01.1, http://www.bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/diagnostics/DIAGV100/CC01A_1410_Limited_CPU_Instruction_Test.pdf

refuted.claim: insttest.cor touches up to address 79,998, so it needs a full 80K machine.
refuted.why: The bytes at 79990-79998 decode to the literal string 'THE END!!'. It is data, never executed and never referenced by any instruction I found. Excluding it, the highest non-blank position in insttest.cor is 11,641, and the highest in ilentest.cor is 33,335 (also literal address-pattern constants 11111/22222/33333, not code). The executable content of insttest.cor lives in 00000-02968 with operand fields in 10001-10600.
refuted.correction: insttest.cor's tests need roughly 12K of storage, not 80K. What forces 80K is the file's own 5-digit header ('80000') plus Jaeger's LoadCore, which warns and clamps if the file's declared core size exceeds the simulator's. Under SIMH, `set cpu 80k` is still the right thing to do before injecting the image, but do not report 80K as a property of the tests themselves - a 20K strict 1410 would run every case in insttest.cor except the decorative string.
refuted.source: Decoded https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cube1us/1410/master/Core/insttest.cor: non-blank positions 0-79998, tail run 79990-79998 = 'THE END!!', preceding non-blank at 11641; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cube1us/1410/master/UI1410CPUT.cpp T1410CPU::LoadCore (clamp when loadCoresize > CPU->coresize)

refuted.why: True only of cc01.cor. I checked the raw 4-byte values: cc01.cor fills unused storage with 0x00000040 (space with the parity C bit set, a valid character). insttest.cor and ilentest.cor fill unused storage with 0x00000000 - no C bit, i.e. a parity-INVALID character in Jaeger's own encoding (BCD_SPACE is defined as 0|BITC). Value histograms: cc01.cor most common raw value 64 (2329 positions) then 74; insttest.cor most common 0 (77,191 positions); ilentest.cor most common 0 (78,936 positions).
refuted.correction: The .cor fill value is per-file, not a format constant. An emulator that validates parity on fetch or on B-cycle read will process-check on insttest.cor and ilentest.cor the moment it touches untouched storage; a loader must decide whether to normalise 0x00 to 0x40 on load. cc01.cor needs no such normalisation.
refuted.source: Direct decode of https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cube1us/1410/master/Core/cc01.cor, insttest.cor, ilentest.cor; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cube1us/1410/master/ubcd.h '#define BCD_SPACE (0 | BITC)', BITC 0x40

additions.claim: The channel prefix character in a 1410/7010 I/O instruction's x-control field is % for channel 1, lozenge for channel 2, ? for channel 3, ! for channel 4; the matching branch-on-I/O-channel-status op codes are R (ch1), X (ch2), 3 (ch3), 1 (ch4). This is the single cleanest strict-1410 discriminator available at the instruction level: a strict 1410 must reject ? and ! prefixes and the 3 and 1 branch ops outright, and reject the lozenge prefix and X unless channel 2 (and therefore processing overlap) is installed.
additions.source: IBM 1410/7010 Operating Guide C28-0351-5 http://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/C28-0351-5_1410_operGuide.pdf p.7 ('"c" is: % - channel 1 / [lozenge] - channel 2 / ? - channel 3 / ! - channel 4' and '"r" is: R - channel 1 / X - channel 2'); CC01A p.004 load instructions RL%B..., XL[lozenge]B..., 3L?B..., 1L!B...; IBM A22-0526-3 p.36 'All use the R op code for channel 1 or the X op code for channel 2'; corroborated in code by https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rcornwell/sims/master/I7000/i7010_defs.h OP_IO1 CHR_R, OP_IO2 CHR_X, OP_IO3 CHR_3, OP_IO4 CHR_1

additions.claim: note1410.txt contains a SECOND label error beyond the '(M)' Multiply slip, and this one changes what the test is actually testing. Line '02848  Move D=T (RL, SCAN, Stop on BWM)' names the wrong d-character: the core image at 02848 holds `D 10517 10519 -`, i.e. d = '-' (BCD 32, B bit only, no 8/4/2/1 bits). Per A22-0526-3 Figure 19 that is 'Blank (No 1, 2, or 4 Bit) = Scan for word marks, record marks, or group-mark-word-marks' with 'NO 8-BIT (RIGHT TO LEFT) B-Bit Only = Stop transfer or scan at B-field word mark'. So Jaeger's prose description is right and his d-character label is wrong; T (BCD 19) would be a right-to-left character move stopping at the A-field word mark, which is the separate test at 02884.

insttest.cor 02800-02968 is the single most valuable oracle in the repo for the ambiguities this project cares about: 16 Move instructions covering the full d-character control matrix with expected results annotated in note1410.txt. The manual's rule set (A22-0526-3 Figure 19) is: bit 1 = transfer numeric portion, bit 2 = transfer zone portion, bit 4 = transfer word marks from A to B, no 1/2/4 bit = scan only (no data transferred). With the 8 bit ON (left-to-right move): no B and no A = stop at first word mark sensed in either field; A only = stop at A-field record mark; B only = stop at A-field group-mark-word-mark; B and A = stop at A-field record mark or group-mark-word-mark. With the 8 bit OFF (right-to-left move): no B and no A = transfer or scan only one storage position; A only = stop at A-field word mark; B only = stop at B-field word mark; B and A = stop at first word mark sensed in either field. I spot-checked all 16 d-characters in the image against this table and every one is consistent (J, K, L, P, '-', '3', L, T, C, C, ',', '$', '.', '=', '='), the sole discrepancy being the 02848 label above.
additions.source: IBM 1410 Principles of Operation A22-0526-3, http://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/A22-0526-3_1410_princOps.pdf, Figure 19 'd-Character Control Bits for Move Instructions' and Figure 20 'Address Registers after Move Operations' (p.25); cross-checked against decoded insttest.cor 02800-02968 and note1410.txt's expected results

additions.claim: Console/printer text diffing between Jaeger's simulator and SIMH i7010 will produce spurious differences in 6 of the 64 code positions, because the two ASCII rendering tables disagree even though the underlying 6-bit code order is identical. Jaeger vs SIMH: 15 (radical) '{' vs 's'; 26 (record mark) '|' vs 'x'; 29 (word separator) '~' vs '`'; 31 (segment mark) '"' vs '_'; 47 (delta) '_' vs '^'; 63 (group mark) '}' vs '|'. All other 58 positions agree exactly, including 12 -> apostrophe (@) and 28 -> '(' (%). This also settles the finder's open question about blanks: both tables put a real space at code 000 and the letter 'b' substitute blank at code 020, so SIMH's CHR_ABLANK is the printable blank and CHR_BLANK is the substitute blank - the same convention Jaeger uses.
additions.source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cube1us/1410/master/ubcd.cpp bcd_ascii[64] vs https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rcornwell/sims/master/I7000/i7010_sys.c mem_to_ascii[64], compared position by position

additions.claim: The finder's open question about CC01A's entry point is answerable: IAR = 02000 is right. Three independent confirmations. (1) The Introduction to Diagnostics states the final execute card 'causes a Branch Out of the load routine to the first instruction of the actual diagnostic program. (Address 02000)'. (2) cc01.cor holds a word-marked N (No-Op) at exactly 02000, and CC01A's flow chart on page 006 begins with 'NO-OP instruction'. (3) cc01.cor itself contains an explicit `J 02000` at 08994, immediately followed by a halt, as the restart path.
additions.source: http://www.bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/diagnostics/DIAGV100/1410_7010_Introduction_to_Diagnostics.pdf p.003 section II.A.4; decoded https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cube1us/1410/master/Core/cc01.cor position 02000 (word-marked N, followed at 02002 by the 64-character collating pattern) and position 08994 (`J 02000` then `.`); the normal-completion path is `J 01972` at 08980, and 01972 is blank in the image

additions.claim: The finder's open question about C020/C021 is answerable: the full CPU tests CC01 was cut down from ARE on bitsavers. C020B_1410_CPU_Error_Detection.pdf (6.4M) is in /pdf/ibm/1410/diagnostics/DIAGV202-K2/, C021B_1410_7010_CPU_Error_Detection.pdf is in DIAGV201/, and C022D_1410_Alarm_Program.pdf is in DIAGV200/. These are the write-ups CC01A p.004 points at ('it may be possible that TC50 will work and be able to bring into Core C020 or C021 to completely check out CPU instructions and give the CE the benefit of different Loops and Options').

DIAGV100/listings.pdf (248K, 3 pages) is not a program listing - it is the scanned printout index of the diagnostic MASTER TAPE ('NEW-0002 / E2-NEW MASTER TAPE', hand-dated 3-8-65). It maps tape record numbers to diagnostic IDs and revision levels: R 001 CC01A, R 005 TC50C, R 011/012/013/014 C020B, R 021 C021B, R 025 C022D, R 051 CU01C, R 055 CU06B, R 061 CU25A, R 065 CU26A, R 073 CU02C, R 080 CU50A, R 090-099 CS30A-CS39A, R 151 ST02D, R 171/172 ST81A, R 201-209 T020C/T021C/T022D, R 251 MP01C, R 259 M003E, R 279 M011A, R 283 M012A, R 287 M013B, R 291 M014B, ... R 951 UP51B. Two practical consequences: CC01A is record 001 (first program on the tape, exactly consistent with 'runs prior to the Tape Control Program'), and UP51 - the utility the CC01A cover credits with punching the card-only deck - is itself record 951 on the same tape.
additions.source: http://www.bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/diagnostics/DIAGV100/listings.pdf, all 3 pages read as images (no text layer; pdftotext yields 3 bytes)

additions.claim: CC01A page 003 names the exact instruction subset the load program depends on, which is a useful minimum-viable-CPU target: 'The Load Program utilizes a few instructions to Load CC01 and they are: BCE, MRCW, MLCS, BA1, RT, BEX1, MLCWA and a Branch instruction.' Page 003 also adds 'This test will only be used in conjunction with the Tape Control Program operating from tape' and 'CC01 will operate on any 1410/7010 system unless an Engineering Change modifies the operations of the standard Instruction set.'

SIMH's memory-size menu offers 30K, 50K, 70K and 90K, which are not valid configurations of either machine (1410: 10/20/40/60/80K; 7010: 40/60/80/100K). Only 10K, 20K, 40K, 60K and 80K are strict-1410-legal, so a validation harness should refuse the others rather than treat the SIMH menu as authoritative.
additions.source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rcornwell/sims/master/I7000/i7010_cpu.c cpu_mod MEMAMOUNT(0..9) = 10K..100K; IBM A22-0526-3 p.5; IBM A22-6726 7010 PrincOps storage capacities

additions.claim: SIMH's cpu_dep already masks a deposited value to `val & (077 | WM)`, so the raw 4-byte little-endian integer from a .cor file can be fed straight into a `d <addr> <val>` line without pre-stripping the 0x40 parity bit - the simulator drops it. Also, cpu_set_size zeroes M[] from the new MEMSIZE up to MAXMEMSIZE and prompts 'Really truncate memory [N]?' if anything above the new size is non-zero, so the size must be set before any image is injected.

A strict-1410 detail worth encoding in the emulator and worth knowing before diffing against SIMH: on input, the 1410 substitutes an asterisk (*) in core storage for any character arriving with incorrect parity, whereas the 1401 silently corrects the parity bit. SIMH i7010 carries an 'ASTRISK' (astmode) CPU register, and the 1410/7010 operating guide's initialization tables all carry the note 'The Asterisk-Insert switch must be set to ON.'
additions.source: IBM A22-0526-3 http://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/A22-0526-3_1410_princOps.pdf, 1401-compatibility appendix, 'Input Characters Having Incorrect Parity': 'The 1401 system corrects any input character of incorrect parity by adding or removing the C bit ... The 1410 system inserts an asterisk (*) in core storage in place of all input characters having incorrect parity.'; C28-0351-5 p.7 Tables I and II notes; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rcornwell/sims/master/I7000/i7010_cpu.c cpu_reg ASTRISK/astmode

additions.claim: cc01.cor's branch-on-word-mark test works by storing op codes WITHOUT word marks and setting them at run time, so a loader that helpfully 'fixes' missing word marks on op codes will silently break the test. Concretely: 02181 holds `J 02226` with no word mark, and the instruction at 02188 is `, 02181` (chained Set Word Mark) which creates it; the same pattern repeats at 02234/02241. A .cor loader must copy the WM bit verbatim and must not infer word marks from instruction boundaries.
additions.source: Decoded https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cube1us/1410/master/Core/cc01.cor 02180-02250, cross-read against http://www.bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/diagnostics/DIAGV100/CC01A_1410_Limited_CPU_Instruction_Test.pdf listing PAGE 3 (PDF p.11), where the corresponding source lines are LABEL AJ / OPCOD B / OPERAND AJ and OPCOD SW / OPERAND *-12 under the comment 'THIS BR NOT TAKEN FIRST TIME THRU' / 'TEST AC FOR WORD MARK'

notes:
Method: a prior session had already mirrored the SIMH sources (i7010_cpu.c, i7010_chan.c, i7010_sys.c, i7000_defs.h, i7010_defs.h, scp.c, STATUS.txt, i7010_test.ini), the Jaeger sources and core images (UI1410CPUT.cpp, ubcd.cpp/.h, note1410.txt, cc01.cor, insttest.cor, ilentest.cor), and the IBM PDFs into the scratchpad, so every code and core-image claim was re-checked against a local copy rather than a fetch. I wrote a fresh independent decoder (5-byte ASCII header, little-endian ints, low 6 bits through bcd_ascii, 0x80 = word mark) rather than trusting the finder's decode.

Opcode/format spot-checks performed against the manual's own instruction descriptions, well past the requested 10: op-code characters and instruction lengths for A, S, ?, !, @, %, D, Z, E, C, T, J/X/R, B, W, V, G, ',', lozenge, /, . and the I/O group M/L/U/K/F/4/2 (21 rows) from A22-0526-3 instruction forms and Timing 'L =' lines; plus all 16 Move d-character rows in insttest.cor 02800-02968 against Figure 19's control-bit and termination table. That pass produced the two biggest corrections in this report (the instruction-length generalisation, and the 02848 d-character mislabel).

1401-vs-1410 hunt: the findings were mostly clean on this - note1410's op characters are 1410 (J for branch, D for move, M for the I/O move), not 1401 (B, M, ...). The one real conflation is the '1402 Load key' claim about card boot; the Load key is a 7010 feature and a strict 1410 IPLs by hand-keying 00000-00011, which C28-0351-5 states explicitly. A softer one: Jaeger's own ubcd.cpp comment describes his table as 'the order of the 1401 BCD codes' - that is fine because 1401 and 1410 share the code, but it should not be cited as a 1410 source.

Could not verify / still open: (1) ilentst2.cor was not in the local mirror, so its size and backup status rest on the finder's GitHub tree-API read alone. (2) Nobody has produced a pass/fail transcript of cc01.cor under any simulator - I confirmed the entry point and the completion path but did not execute it, so the halt-address-to-routine oracle is still theoretical. (3) The CC01A listing has no OCR layer (48 pages, PDF 1.3, 2002 Acrobat import; pdftotext returns 48 bytes of whitespace) and no OCR tooling was available in this environment (no tesseract, no ocrmypdf), so I verified the listing by reading four pages as images (cover, 003, 004, 005, and listing PAGE 3 at PDF p.11) and did not attempt the remaining ~38. Transcribing the halt-address table remains manual work. (4) I did not test whether rcornwell's i7010 actually accepts a synthesised L1-format deck - that would need a build and a run.

One workflow note for the implementer that falls out of the above: the finder's recommended plan is sound, but two of its premises need adjusting. Do not size the machine at 80K because of insttest.cor's tests (they fit in 12K; size it 80K only to match the file header), and normalise the 0x00 fill in insttest.cor/ilentest.cor to 0x40 if the emulator parity-checks storage on read.
